items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: I had a chance to play with him a lot and get my butt kicked from him as well.

ctx.x: I mean you do a lot of educational work?

I do a lot of education but I don’t have any full time teaching position. I’m presently the adjunct processor of jazz saxophone at Amherst College. And I have a handful of students every semester. But for me, I really love jazz ed — I love jazz teaching and being in that world. I had a lot of incredible mentors when I was a teenager growing up. I had — when I was growing up on Long Island there was an alto saxophone-clarinet-flute player named Joe Dixon who was a — he played with Bunny Berrigan and Artie Shaw,…

for young musicians to have that experience, and because of the demise of touring big bands, you know the apprenticeship system is kind of disappearing. So young musicians coming out of college are forced to kind of really create their own situation and create their own scene.
